items.caption: This Shuowen-style seal-script form of 常 shows 尚 above 巾, the components traditionally analyzed as phonetic and semantic, respectively. The character is glossed as a lower garment in the received Shuowen account.
items.alt: Black seal-script 常, with a compact upper section above a long, enclosed lower section, on a white background.
items.selection_reason: This is the only clearly identified 常 glyph in the candidates. Its visible structure complements the received component analysis and garment gloss, while the modern redraw does not establish the earliest form or independently prove the analysis.

limitations.text: This image is a modern redraw in Shuowen seal-script style, not an ancient inscription. The cited sources support a traditional analysis of 尚 as phonetic and 巾 as semantic, but the drawing alone cannot establish the character’s origin or earliest meaning.

Specialist sources report garment uses in bronze and Warring States materials, but the consulted evidence does not date those artifacts or establish which attestation is earliest. The transition from the garment sense to later meanings is not fully dated.
